title: Enhanced antihypertensive efficacy of selenium‐enriched black tea is associated with galloylated catechin enrichment: integrating chemical profiling, molecular modeling, and animal studies
content:
Abstract

Background

Selenium-enriched tea has been reported to exhibit enhanced antihypertensive efficacy; however, the key bioactive constituents and their molecular targets remain undefined. To elucidate the relationship between selenium-induced compositional alterations and antihypertensive effects, we employed a high-salt diet-induced hypertensive rat model combined with chemical profiling, network pharmacology, and molecular dynamics simulations.

Results

Selenium biofortification of the tea plant increased the contents of galloylated catechins (epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) and epicatechin gallate (ECG)) in the resulting black tea. In hypertensive rats, selenium-enriched black tea (Se-BT) exhibited superior antioxidative, anti-inflammatory, and antihypertensive effects compared with conventional black tea (BT), increasing serum endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS) activity and nitric oxide (NO) levels (+39.32% and +12.20%, respectively, compared with BT). Network pharmacology identified galloylated catechins (EGCG, ECG, and gallocatechin gallate (GCG)) as major bioactive constituents associated with hypertension, and KEGG (Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes) enrichment pointed to pathways converging on eNOS-mediated NO signaling. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations suggested that galloylated catechins preferentially occupy a common binding pocket adjacent to the eNOS BH4-binding region and that EGCG, as the representative galloylated catechin, maintained a stable binding mode throughout the simulation.

Conclusion

Selenium enrichment enhances the antihypertensive efficacy of black tea, primarily through the accumulation of galloylated catechins. These findings suggest that the stable binding of galloylated catechins to eNOS may provide a structural basis for the experimentally observed enhancement of eNOS activity and NO production. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.
